Melodic Diatonic Intervals.heading: Hear two notes. Name the distance.
Melodic Diatonic Intervals.intro: You will hear two notes, one after the other. Choose the name of the distance between them.

steps.title: Listen to the two notes
steps.description: Press Play to hear the first note followed by the second. Notice how far apart they sound. You can listen again whenever you need to.

steps.title: Choose the interval
steps.description: An interval is the distance between two notes. Select the answer that matches what you hear, such as Major 3rd.

steps.title: Submit your answer
steps.description: When you are ready, press Submit Answer. You can change your choice before you submit.

Melodic Diatonic Intervals.about: An interval names how far apart two notes are. This quiz focuses on major and perfect intervals. An octave is the distance from a note to the next higher note with the same name, such as C to the next C. “Melodic” means the two notes play one after the other.
Melodic Diatonic Intervals.exampleExplanation: In this visual example, C and E are a major 3rd apart. Choose Major 3rd for that distance. During the quiz, listen for the distance between the notes you hear; the notes may have different names.

Harmonic Diatonic Intervals.heading: Two notes together. Name the distance.
Harmonic Diatonic Intervals.intro: You will hear two notes at the same time. Choose the name of the distance between them.

steps.title: Listen to the two notes
steps.description: Press Play to hear both notes together. Try to hear the lower sound and the higher sound. You can listen again whenever you need to.

steps.title: Choose the interval
steps.description: An interval is the distance between two notes. Select the answer that matches what you hear, such as Major 3rd.

steps.title: Submit your answer
steps.description: When you are ready, press Submit Answer. You can change your choice before you submit.
